text: This lesson teaches no new technology — just five wrong-answer patterns that repeat across every DP-700 domain, so you recognize them under time pressure instead of meeting them cold on exam day.
Trap one: similar-sounding item types get swapped, like Lakehouse for Warehouse. Trap two: the exam wants the simple, native Fabric answer, not an option that bolts on an external Azure service.
Absolute words like 'always' or 'never' are usually bait. The qualifier at the end of a stem often flips the answer. And picking a real but broader-than-needed control is the most common trap of all.
Every trap has the same shape: the wrong option is real, technically correct somewhere else, and just not what this scenario asked for.
Five traps, one exam. Next up: turning this pattern recognition into an actual week-by-week study plan.
